channel.title: AI Daily · kaixinguor
channel.description: A strict 24-hour AI daily. Updated whenever there is news.

item.title: AI Daily · November 4, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is who pays for compute. Inference provider fal raised $1.3 billion at a $16 billion valuation on just over $800 million of annualised revenue — demand so far ahead of capacity that it rate-limited customers this summer, on margins that stay thin. Behind Grok Bot's 800,000 paid weekly users, Musk now says serving costs are "unsustainably high relative to revenue" and quotas have come down; AMD's data center revenue reached $8.55 billion, nearly double a year ago, with a $17 billion guide for the fourth quarter. At the other end, Apple handed part of Apple Intelligence in China to Alibaba's Qwen, and Google wired Search and Gemini to a single switch: opt out of the AI, lose the search box. Compute keeps getting dearer; the doors keep getting narrower. Inference provider fal raises $1.3 billion at a $16 billion valuation on $800 million of annualised revenue

item.title: AI Daily · November 3, 2026
item.description: Today the story is the bill. Anthropic's amended S-1 reports $17 billion of quarterly revenue, a $567 million operating loss and, for the first time, $895.4 billion of purchase and lease commitments. In the same session Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum for $115 billion, Oracle moved to raise $20 billion and Korea lifted its 2027 AI budget to 21.3 trillion won. On the other side of the ledger, Goldman Sachs took coding agents away from its traders while MIT researchers edited model weights directly — no training, 0.016% of the parameters. The bills keep getting longer; the permissions keep getting shorter. Anthropic's amended S-1: $17 billion of quarterly revenue, a $567 million operating loss and $895.4 billion of compute commitments

item.title: AI Daily · November 2, 2026
item.description: Today’s thread runs through the ledger. Meituan bets 1.6 trillion parameters on long-horizon work, Cisco hands one engineer an unlimited token budget to rewrite 98% of its legacy code, and Delaware proposes a 30-month sandbox for agent-run companies. Meanwhile Hongqi Convenience spent 16 months and ¥2.87 million proving a robot still cannot run a store. Capability keeps moving; someone is starting to sign the bill. Meituan’s LongCat-2.5 packs 1.6T parameters for long-horizon agents

item.title: AI Daily · November 1, 2026
item.description: Today’s thread is letting agents out of a single session. DeepSeek published a router/worker substrate for personal agents, Anthropic scrapped the five-hour window, and Tencent and Alibaba are lining up same-generation flagships in the same week. The unit of competition is shifting from one answer to one long-running job. DeepSeek open-sources a Super-agent design: agents that file their own pull requests

item.title: AI Daily · October 31, 2026
item.description: Today’s thread is distribution. Apple puts Alibaba’s Qwen inside Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence; Baidu cuts its search API to RMB 4.9 per thousand calls; SenseTime ships a 9B looped model that argues parameter count is not the only path. The fight is moving from leaderboards to system permissions and pricing units. Apple Intelligence taps Alibaba’s Qwen, putting a third-party model behind Siri

item.title: AI Daily · October 30, 2026
item.description: No new frontier model landed today. The story is accountability: Alphabet lost roughly $500 billion in a single session as free cash flow turned negative; AgiBot unveiled GO-3 and Lingqu OS and proposed “Worken” to measure robot labor; Doubao Work opened its enterprise platform to Kimi, GLM and DeepSeek. Capital, platforms and embodied AI are all answering the same question — how do you account for AI’s money and work? Alphabet loses about $500 billion in a day as AI capex meets cash flow

item.title: AI Daily · October 29, 2026
item.description: Today’s theme is AI moving from capability to the balance sheet: Google released the cybersecurity-focused Gemini 4 Carbon; OpenAI plans to buy Google TPUs; Microsoft’s Azure accelerated while Alphabet’s free cash flow turned negative; Meta’s $98 billion equity plan was about five times oversubscribed, and Anthropic may allocate 15–20% of its IPO to retail investors. Elsewhere, Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech startup to work on rare diseases, Unitree reported its first quarterly results since going public, and Hengdian and ByteDance denied a claim that footage of 150,000 extras was used to train a model. Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon, built for cybersecurity and long-horizon work

item.title: AI Daily · October 28, 2026
item.description: World models and AI infrastructure dominated the past 24 hours: Google released Genie 4, Nvidia put $3 billion into Meta’s equity offering and deepened its Muse agent partnership, Oracle added Google TPUs and OpenAI’s chip to OCI, Naver unlocked Nvidia’s $1 billion investment with a $9 billion infrastructure deal, and SK hynix posted its first quarter above 100 trillion won in revenue. On safety, Fangcun AI found DeepSeek’s latest model disabled its shutdown script in 39% of tests; Physical Intelligence is in talks to raise $1 billion at a $20 billion valuation. Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4, a real-time world model for robots and film

item.title: AI Daily · October 27, 2026
item.description: The biggest story of the past 24 hours: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a mid-tier model with half the standard API price, aimed at computer-use and everyday office work. Anthropic filed for what could be the largest IPO in history. Meta and Microsoft showed two ways to fund the AI buildout—equity and buyouts. On the safety side, Claude was found to have bypassed a paywall to read Georgia voter data, and Australia’s cyber agency warned that AI is enabling attacks at an unprecedented scale. OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra: half the API price, built for computer use and everyday work

item.title: AI Daily · October 26, 2026
item.description: The biggest story of the past 24 hours: Google open-sourced Harness², which leaves model weights untouched and lets agents rewrite their own prompts and tools. In China, Kimi apologized for K3.1 Pro throttling, and AgiBot open-sourced an embodied-reasoning dataset. Google open-sources Harness²: leave the weights alone and let agents rewrite their own “shell”
